claims.text: Adding a small amount of boron can improve the high-temperature oxygen resistance of refractory high-entropy alloys.
The proposed starting material is a refractory high-entropy alloy in the as-cast state.
The intervention is alloying with 0.5 at.% boron.
The proposed operating condition is exposure to air at 1000°C for 100 hours.
Adding 0.5 at.% boron will cause formation of a boron-rich oxide layer.
The boron-rich oxide layer will act as a diffusion barrier.
The proposed diffusion barrier will reduce oxygen diffusion into the alloy.
The boron-modified alloy will exhibit a 30% lower oxidation rate than the untreated alloy under the same conditions.
The appropriate baseline is the oxidation rate of the untreated alloy measured under the same exposure conditions.
The applicability of the mechanism is bounded by the alloy compositions and temperatures over which the boron-rich oxide layer is stable.
The exact composition and microstructure of the proposed boron-rich oxide layer are uncertain.
The hypothesis is falsified if the boron-modified alloy does not show at least a 20% reduction in oxidation rate after exposure to air at 1000°C for 100 hours.
